condition_specific: Bladder cancer (12 yrs), brain cancer (10 yrs), breast cancer (5 yrs, age <40, no genetic predisposition), cervical cancer (15 yrs), colorectal cancer (10 yrs), esophageal cancer (10 yrs), kidney cancer (15 yrs), leukemia (5 yrs), lung cancer (4 yrs), mesothelioma/asbestosis (10 yrs), multiple myeloma (15 yrs), non-Hodgkin's lymphoma (15 yrs), testicular cancer (10 yrs)
post_termination_formula: Disease must manifest within 10 years of last date engaged in firefighting activities; individual disease minimums range from 4–15 years of employment
filing_deadline_notes: Claim must be filed as soon as firefighter knows or should have known condition resulted from presumptive occupational disease
notes: Tobacco exclusion: the firefighter may not be a regular user of tobacco products, must not have a history of regular tobacco use in the 10 years preceding the claim, and must not have been exposed by a cohabitant who regularly used tobacco in the home for 10+ years before diagnosis. Employment history is calculated starting July 1, 2014 only (§ 39-71(3)). Volunteer firefighters are covered only if their employer opts in and the insurer agrees to provide presumptive coverage (§ 39-71(1)(b)). Total claim payment is capped at $5 million per claim. A pre-employment exam is required within 90 days of hiring, with subsequent exams at least every 2 years. Lung cancer and myocardial infarction must be of a type that can be caused by firefighting activities. Most of this list (11 of the 13 cancer types — all except non-Hodgkin's lymphoma and testicular cancer) took effect July 1, 2019 (SB 160, Ch. 158, L. 2019). Non-Hodgkin's lymphoma (15-year service requirement) and testicular cancer (10-year service requirement) were added four years later by SB 310 (Ch. 442, L. 2023), signed May 4, 2023, with an effective date presumed to be October 1, 2023 under Montana's default effective-date statute (§ 1-2-201, MCA); the exact effective-date clause within SB 310's own bill text has not been independently confirmed.
